title: David makes Jerusalem his capital
description: According to the Hebrew Bible, King David takes Jerusalem from the Jebusites and rules a united kingdom from it.

title: Fall of Samaria
description: Assyria conquers the northern kingdom of Israel and deports many of its people.

title: Destruction of the First Temple
description: Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon takes Jerusalem, destroys Solomon's Temple and deports much of Judah's population; some scholars date it to 586 BCE.

title: Cyrus allows the exiles to return
description: After conquering Babylon, Cyrus of Persia permits the Judean exiles to go home and rebuild their temple, according to the Book of Ezra.

title: Second Temple completed
description: The rebuilt temple in Jerusalem is dedicated under Persian rule.

title: Maccabean Revolt begins
description: Judeans led by the priest Mattathias and his sons rise against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV, who had banned Jewish practice.

title: Temple rededicated
description: Judas Maccabeus retakes Jerusalem and purifies the Temple, the event remembered at Hanukkah.

title: Pompey takes Jerusalem
description: The Roman general Pompey captures the city, and Judea becomes a client state of Rome.

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
description: Roman forces under Titus take Jerusalem during the First Jewish–Roman War and burn the Temple.

title: Fall of Masada
description: The last rebel fortress of the First Jewish–Roman War falls to the Romans.

title: Bar Kokhba revolt crushed
description: Rome puts down the last great Judean revolt at Betar, and Jews are barred from Jerusalem; the war began in 132 and by some accounts ended in 136.

title: Mishnah compiled
description: Judah ha-Nasi edits the oral law into the Mishnah, the base text of rabbinic Judaism.

title: Muslim conquest of Jerusalem
description: The city surrenders to the Rashidun Caliphate after a siege, ending Byzantine rule.

title: Crusaders take Jerusalem
description: The First Crusade storms the city and kills many of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants.

title: Saladin takes Jerusalem
description: After his victory at Hattin, Saladin receives the surrender of Jerusalem from the Crusaders.

title: Jews expelled from England
description: Edward I orders all Jews to leave England; they are not readmitted until the 1650s.

title: Alhambra Decree
description: Ferdinand and Isabella order the Jews of Castile and Aragon to convert or leave, ending the largest Jewish community of medieval Europe.

title: Jews made citizens in France
description: The National Constituent Assembly grants full citizenship to the Jews of France, the first such emancipation in Europe.

title: Pogroms in the Russian Empire
description: A wave of anti-Jewish riots after the assassination of Alexander II begins the mass emigration of Jews from the Russian Empire.

title: Rishon LeZion founded
description: Jewish immigrants from the Russian Empire found one of the first farming settlements of the First Aliyah.

title: First Zionist Congress
description: Convened by Theodor Herzl, the congress founds the Zionist Organization and calls for a home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

title: Tel Aviv founded
description: Sixty-six families draw lots for plots in the dunes north of Jaffa.

title: Balfour Declaration
description: The British government declares its support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

title: British forces enter Jerusalem
description: The city surrenders to General Allenby's army, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Mandate for Palestine approved
description: The Council of the League of Nations confirms British rule in Palestine with the terms of the Balfour Declaration written in.

title: Nuremberg Laws
description: Germany strips Jews of citizenship and forbids marriage between Jews and other Germans.

title: Kristallnacht
description: In a night of organised attacks across Germany and Austria, synagogues are burned and about 30,000 Jewish men are sent to concentration camps.

title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
description: Jewish fighters resist the final deportation from the ghetto for nearly a month.

title: Auschwitz liberated
description: Soviet troops reach the largest of the German killing centres, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered.

title: UN partition plan adopted
place: Flushing Meadows, New York, United States
description: The General Assembly votes to divide Palestine into a Jewish and an Arab state; fighting breaks out the next day.

title: Israel declares independence
description: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel as the British mandate ends, and neighbouring Arab states invade the next day.

title: Suez Crisis
description: Israel invades Sinai in concert with Britain and France, and withdraws under American and Soviet pressure.

title: Eichmann trial opens
description: Adolf Eichmann, an organiser of the deportations, is tried in Jerusalem and hanged the following year.

title: Six-Day War
description: Israel defeats Egypt, Jordan and Syria in six days and takes Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights.

title: Yom Kippur War
description: Egypt and Syria attack on the holiest day of the Jewish year, and Israel recovers after early losses.

title: Peace treaty with Egypt
description: Following the Camp David Accords, Egypt becomes the first Arab state to recognise Israel, which returns Sinai.

title: First Intifada begins
description: A Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation starts in Gaza and spreads to the West Bank.

title: Oslo Accord signed
description: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization recognise each other and agree on Palestinian self-rule in stages.

title: Rabin assassinated
description: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin is shot by an Israeli opponent of the Oslo Accords after a peace rally.

title: Second Intifada begins
description: Violence follows Ariel Sharon's visit to the Temple Mount and lasts more than four years.

title: Withdrawal from Gaza
description: Israel removes its settlers and troops from the Gaza Strip.
